title: Guesstimate question pool
description: The contract for data/questions.json. Enforced by pipeline/import_questions.py on every import; the numbers themselves are separately re-derived from the source datasets by pipeline/verify_questions.py. Schema validity means the shape is right, NOT that the stats are true — both gates have to pass before content ships.

id.description: Stable, unique, kebab-case. Convention: <league>-<xstat><ystat>-<player>[-<season>]. Never reuse an id for different content — a player's stats history is keyed on it.

targetPlayer.description: Full name. Append a season for season-scoped questions: 'Derrick Henry, 2020' (NFL/MLB) or 'Baron Davis, 2003-04' (NBA). The chart strips the season from the dot label; the prompt above it already states the season.

referencePlayers.description: Plotted, named, with their values listed under the chart. Two is thin; three is the house standard. Must be distinct people — two seasons of the same player as separate dots reads as a bug.

fact.description: The reveal payload, and the actual product — it is the only thing in this genre that teaches you something. Should explain WHY the answer is counterintuitive, not restate the numbers. Existing content runs 280-610 characters; the 700 ceiling is a guard against a pasted wall of text, not a target.

source.description: Named source for every number in this question. A dataset citation must identify the dataset and the aggregation (e.g. 'nflverse-data player_stats release, regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season').

step.description: Guess snapping granularity, in stat units. 1 for whole-number stats (All-Star counts, home runs), 0.1 for per-game rates, 0.001 for batting average. Defaults to 0.1 if omitted. Getting this wrong collapses the usable chart: a fixed 0.1 step on batting average leaves only two clickable values across the whole axis.

domain.description: [min, max] plotted range. MUST NOT be derived from the answer — deriving bounds from the target leaks it, which was a real shipped bug (COMPETITIVE_ANALYSIS.md §2). Prefer round numbers four tick-steps wide so the axis labels read cleanly.
